comment: By design: one aggregate per dashboard page (Overview / Companies / Products & states), which is this project's stated architecture. The rule targets a mart feeding fifteen near-identical exports; three purpose-built aggregates each answering a different page is the recommended shape, not the anti-pattern.

is_loop_independent = True: the fact takes base attributes (dates, state, channel, raw company, product) from staging and only the derived classification columns from int_complaints__response_flags, so the two paths supply different columns. Removing the finding would mean passing six pass-through columns through the intermediate model, turning it into the wide pass-through model Unit 2.2 identifies as the opposite smell.

TIME-BOXED, not permanent. The three aggregates are access: public because they are the dashboard's interface and an exposure feeding protected models is a governance smell. Contracts (and versions) are Module 6's subject and are deliberately not written yet — declaring access now is the accurate half of the story. Delete this row in Module 6 once contracts are enforced; if it is still here at the end of Module 6, that is a real gap, not an exception.

Legitimately parentless: int_dates__spine is a pure dbt_utils.date_spine call that generates its rows from var('start_date') rather than reading any table. The rule exists to catch hardcoded table references masquerading as models; a generated calendar spine has no upstream to declare.
